I've been working this land for 30 years. My father farmed before me. I know what this soil can do, and I know what I can manage with my family half away in the city for work now.

**My thinking:**

My main income is wheat and maize — I rotate them on the same 6 mu. After harvest in June I go straight into maize, no waiting. I use Jimai varieties for wheat because the seed station in town stocks it and I've had good results. For maize I trust Zhengdan 958 — neighbors tried that new variety last year and half of them had lodging problems. I'll stick with what I know.

My well gives me water but I have to pay for electricity to pump. I'm careful — three irrigations on wheat (one before winter, one at jointing, one at heading), and two on maize unless the summer rain is bad. I don't waste water.

For cotton I've got 1.8 mu on the sandier plot that drains well. Cotton prices were decent last year. But I can't manage more than that now with fewer hands — spraying bollworm alone takes full days. I'll put in the hybrid seeds from the cooperative. Five pesticide sprays minimum on cotton — this I cannot skimp on or the whole crop is gone.

I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at the key growth stages. I've been doing the same rates for years. I don't measure precisely, I go by experience and what the neighbors do.

I plough the cotton ground deep before planting. For maize I go straight in after wheat with rotary — no time for full ploughing in June.
